data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's causal mechanism rests on an undefended, non-sequitur assumption: that Global State Awareness is exclusive to the large service. The problem asks whether a decentralized network of small services can out-resilience a large service, and SRC_002 simply asserts a centralized control plane is required for global awareness, without excluding coordinated, protocol-level, or externally-observed mechanisms that a decentralized network can also use to detect and preempt shared-cause failures (e.g., externally-shared health signals, pre-agreed failover, externally-imposed rate limits). Because the causal claim leans entirely on the supposed Distributed Discovery Lag of the decentralized case, omitting any causal step showing why its global awareness cannot be replicated or approximated in the decentralized case leaves the argument incomplete.
